events.excerpt: Unocoin says crypto left one of its wallets even though it froze its BitGo account in its latest update on the exploit it suffered. Unicoin thinks a backup recovery path in BitGo’s (NYSE: BTGO) multisignature wallets was used to move its funds, but it does not know who the perpetrator is. How did crypto leave a wallet that was frozen? Unocoin asked BitGo to freeze its company accounts on November 6 after it spotted suspicious activity. Its blog says the freezes began at 11:24 UTC for Fireblocks and 11:29 UTC for BitGo. Both custodians confirmed the freezes, and no losses were found at that point. However, on November 13, Unocoin said its money was moved out of the wallet that BitGo confirmed was frozen. Unocoin says BitGo’s multisignature wallets have a backup path that is meant to let a client reach funds even if BitGo goes offline. Unocoin says this path “appears to have been exploited” and that it is now checking how it was reached and used. BitGo’s own documents point fingers at its clients instead. Its Wallet Recovery Wizard lets clients take assets out of their wallets “without BitGo.” It uses the user key and the backup key to move funds to a new address. BitGo’s documents say these recovery transactions “bypass any policies you have with BitGo.” The recovery wizard requir
events.headline: Unocoin says BitGo freeze held, but a backup key let funds leave on-chain

events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks Digital credit is an emerging asset class that transforms corporate Bitcoin balance sheets into income producing securities. Strategy pioneered the market with five perpetual preferred equity instruments: STRK, STRF, STRD, STRC, and STRE (the first four are listed in the U.S.). Strive subsequently introduced SATA and SATS, bringing the category to six U.S. instruments across two issuers. These securities offer investors preferred equity (read: credit-like) exposure to companies whose balance sheets are dominated by Bitcoin. Their perpetual structure means investors principally rely on recurring dividends and the continued financial strength of the issuer. Unlike term debt, there is no maturation date at which the full principal is ever paid back. Evaluating digital credit requires examining four characteristics: creditworthiness, investor protections, liquidity, and dividend profile. This article explains all four dimensions and then offers a ranking for the six digital credit instruments along these lines. None of this should be taken as investment advice—it is only a systematic framework for analyzing digital credit. 1. events.excerpt: This essay is adapted from a keynote speech delivered at the DEF CON 34 conference in Las Vegas on August 7, 2026. The essay originally appeared in CyberScoop . I want to talk about AI hacking. There are three aspects: people hacking AI systems, people using AI to hack other systems, and AIs hacking systems on their own, not even maliciously. The last two matter more than the first. The third is the weirdest and potentially the most destabilizing. I started writing about this in 2021 and in my 2022 book, A Hacker’s Mind . Back then I said it was mostly still science fiction, but not stupid science fiction. We’re seeing it more and more, especially in the past year. The trends I’m describing don’t require a major breakthrough in AI. They’re starting to happen now, and they’ll happen more often as AIs get better at autonomous problem-solving. And it will involve far more than computer code. AI will hack all sorts of social, economic and political systems. It will find vulnerabilities and exploit them. This is a difference in kind, not just degree. We’re not ready for it, and we need to think about the implications now. events.excerpt: Doing board level diagnosis on a PCB is hardly black magic, but some PCBs are definitely more daunting than others. The Socket LGA 1851 mainboard that [Fix the Pixel] got in for repair being one of the harder cases due to the sheer size and complexity. Adding to the excitement was having to purchase a used CPU for it off eBay to even test the board and work through the boot-up sequence to find the culprit. A basic understanding of how these mainboards power up and verify that they can move on to the next phase is essential here, starting with the power rails. Although the culprit turned out to be a single missing 5.1 Ohm resistor on an SPI clock line, you still have to reason your way through the diagnosis. For this mainboard the boardview was fortunately available, but that still doesn’t make it easy to spot components that have quietly left the chat. With the CPU and RAM installed the board doesn’t bother to boot up, with the VRM controller for the CPU’s power phases showing its enable pin to stay low. Going down the list of conditions for this pin to be pulled high the culprit was eventually found, when the PCH – the board’s chipset – never reading the BIOS chip. Checking the SPI lines on the mainboard near the BIOS chip quickly showed the knocked-off resistor on the SPI clock
events.headline: Fixing a Dead Socket LGA 1851 Mainboard with a Resistor

events.excerpt: I love a good Zone 2 ride . There’s nothing like getting on the bike, settling into a groove, and letting the miles (and hours) flow by. But sometimes when I hopped on the Specialized Tarmac SL9 S-Level, Zone 2 would turn into a tempo ride. It was like having a little imp—the stereotype dressed in red with the pitchfork—on my left shoulder whispering into my ear: “Go fast. This bike was built to go fast. Speed is good. You can do a Zone 2 ride tomorrow.” Normally, I'd count on the good imp—the dude with the harp and wings—on my right shoulder to restrain these urges. But the Tarmac is so seductive that he would just shrug and say “he’s got a point.” And in a moment of weakness, I would drop the hammer and head into the red, just because the SL9 makes that so rewarding. The Tarmac SL9 is Specialized’s aero road bike, with the S-Level sitting just below the S-Works in Specialized’s top tier of carbon, aero road bikes, where it replaced the Tarmac SL8 Pro. After it got an update this year, I spent several weeks riding it, putting nearly 1,000 miles on it Specialized offers the Tarmac SL9 in four models, all available with SRAM and Shimano drivetrains (Ars tested the SRAM version). events.excerpt: Those deeply familiar with online gambling know that affiliate marketing is the invisible engine that has kept this industry going since its launch. The sector faces advertising restrictions like no other and relies on third parties to drive traffic to gambling sites, as operators often struggle to do this themselves. The individuals and companies that do this for them, the affiliates, typically follow a simple procedure. They receive a tracking link from an operator, connect it to a button or banner, and every registration logged through it gives them a piece of the wagering activity they helped generate. However, that is just this field in a nutshell. It hides many complexities, which start with the payout models used, volume thresholds, KPIs, and so on. Moreover, affiliate programs and how they work on both sides have greatly evolved over the past decade, and so have the tools and criteria that get used. To better explain all this, and where we are today compared to where we began, we reached out to an affiliate expert, Sebastian Jarosch, the founder of Mithrillium Media Ltd. events.excerpt: Researchers from Hanbat National University and the Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology have come up with a way to boost the efficiency and lifespan of organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displays — with the addition of a thin additional layer designed to prevent the formation of "holes" created by excess positive charges. "Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) are typically affected by nonradiative energy loss originating from interfacial charge accumulation and exciton quenching processes," the researchers explain of their focus in the project. "In particular, spontaneous orientation polarization in organic thin films generates a giant surface potential (GSP), which modifies the interfacial electrostatic environment and induces unintended charge injection and charge accumulation near the emitting layer (EML). These excess charge carriers increase the polaron density in the EML and promote exciton–polaron quenching, which limits device efficiency and stability." To simplify: the efficiency of current OLED display panels is limited owing to an internal molecular alignment causing the gathering of excess positive charges, effective "holes," near the light-emitting layer which then reduce its ability to produce light efficiently. The team's solution: adding electron-blocking l
events.headline: Preventing "Holes" in OLED Displays Can Boost Efficiency and Lifespan, Researchers Find

The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) said on Thursday that it had written to more than 200 senior health leaders across the UK, warning that employees accessing records without good reason put patient privacy and public trust at risk. The ICO received and assessed more than 300 reports of medical record snooping between January and mid-October 2026. Staff were caught looking up people they knew, poking around patient files out of sheer curiosity, and sharing private information with people who had no business seeing it. The figure covers reports submitted by healthcare organizations rather than confirmed breaches, and excludes cases still awaiting assessment. ICO chief executive Paul Arnold wants health bosses to personally assure him that their organizations have safeguards in place to stop staff having a nose through records they aren't supposed to see. events.excerpt: I’d like feedback on a draft ERC that says how a wallet derives hash-based post-quantum keys (leanSPHINCS, SLH-DSA, WOTS, FORS, XMSS) from a BIP-39 phrase. Draft: Add ERC: Hash-Based Key Derivation from BIP-39 by johba37 · Pull Request #2172 · ethereum/ERCs · GitHub Why Contracts already verify hash-based signatures through ERC-1271 and account abstraction, and EIP-8288 would aggregate leanSPHINCS. Users back their accounts up with BIP-39 phrases, but no standard says how a phrase becomes a hash-based key, and implementations have diverged: from the BIP-39 entropy, with Keccak-256 over application labels (the Winterlock signer I work on does this today); through a second PBKDF2 over the phrase with its own salt ( WOTS-39 ); through HMAC-SHA512 over the BIP-39 seed under its own label (a hardware wallet in development). So the same phrase gives different keys in different wallets, and restoring it elsewhere does not restore the keys. A wallet that already has BIP-32 might derive these keys through it. That would bring a problem of its own. Every BIP-32 node has an elliptic-curve public key. events.excerpt: UK police forces must do more to prevent the wrongful arrests of people subjected to retrospective facial recognition (RFR) searches, according to a Criminal Justice Inspectorate that holds deep concerns about the way in which the technology is used. According to a report from His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services (HMICFRS), there is a large gap in understanding among police forces and the National Crime Agency about how RFR should be used in responsible policing. The inspectorate blamed "fragmented and underdeveloped" frameworks for governance and legislation. It pointed to a lack of bespoke legislation to provide a uniform approach to police facial recognition use – and said existing laws have not kept pace with the technology. HMICFRS also said the rules governing each force's use of RFR are mismatched, and called for a statutory code to be included in the forthcoming Police Reform Bill to set nationwide standards. Illustrating the breadth of misunderstanding across forces, the report noted that despite the message being routinely communicated by National Police Chiefs' Council (NPCC) reps, individual investigators "often" thought RFR results constituted evidence rather than intelligence. events.headline: Brit police watchdog says cops' use of facial recog risks wrongful arrests

A second address, 0x01e2, which the analytics platform had earlier described as a “gambler” after it got hit by six liquidations in 12 hours covering 404.86 BTC ($28.9 million), had another 511 BTC worth $36.4 million liquidated when the asset’s price plunged below its November 2021 peak. The third wallet lost a 357.09 BTC position valued at just over $25 million, while the fourth, 0x4a20, which suffered the least damage among the observed whales, had positions in Solana ($9 million), Bitcoin ($5.85 million), and Ethereum ($3.52 million), all wrecked.
